_note: Scoring model + operational configuration. Per-check thresholds live in checks.json, NOT here — one source of truth each. The model is a capability score rather than a penalty score (100 - sum(penalty)): a penalty model is unbounded, double-counts correlated findings, and conflates a missing signal with a negative one.

category_weights._note: Weights for the overall score (a weighted mean of category scores). Equal by design: gating is handled structurally by dependency suppression, not by weight inflation, so no category needs boosting to encode importance. With 3 AI-side categories and 1 human-side, equal weights land at 75% AI / 25% human — matching the brief's 4:1 mechanic split — and require no arbitrary justification.

state_credits._note: Credit awarded per check state. States listed in excluded_states earn no credit AND are removed from the denominator, so an unmeasurable check lowers confidence rather than the score.

suppression._note: Dependency suppression collapses correlated findings: dependents of a failed prerequisite become `unknown` instead of `fail`. require_verified_prerequisite is the anti-dodge rule — a merely heuristic failure may NOT silence dependents, which keeps recall honest and stops suppression being used to duck hard calls.

budgets._note: Global deadline leaves margin under the mandated 5-minute ceiling. Per-request and render timeouts deliberately live in `fetch` and `render` respectively — they were duplicated here and the copies were never read, which is exactly how two copies of one value drift apart.

fetch._contact_url_note: Optional. When set, it is appended as ' (+URL)' to form the User-Agent sent on every request, which is the convention for identifying a crawler to a site operator. It is EMPTY by default on purpose. It previously held 'https://example.com/citely-bot', a domain IANA reserves for documentation, so an operator who investigated the bot landed on a placeholder that read like a real contact. Shipping an invented URL would also breach this project's own rule against presenting an unobserved value as a fact. Set it to a page you actually control.
fetch._allow_private_hosts_note: TEST-ONLY ESCAPE HATCH. Must stay false in every real run. When true, the SSRF guard permits private/loopback addresses and any port, so the E2E suite can audit the localhost fixture server. Enabling it against untrusted input reintroduces full SSRF exposure.
fetch._html_content_types_note: Page content is restricted to text/html. Without enforcement a PDF, JSON API or image would be fetched and parsed as HTML, producing garbage findings on unseen sites.

robots._note: Two DISTINCT robots concerns, deliberately separated. (1) `audit_user_agent_gate`: may CitelyAuditBot fetch at all? Operational only — if disallowed the orchestrator stops, emits one critical finding, and sets partial_reason 'blocked'. Never scored, because nobody blocklists an unknown auditor UA. (2) `ai_crawlers`: may the assistants' crawlers fetch? THIS is the scored signal (check access.ai_crawlers_allowed) — a site can allow us and still be invisible to ChatGPT.

ai_crawlers.powers: the corpus many open LLMs train on

robots._crawler_list_note: Tokens live in config so they can be updated as operators add or rename crawlers, with no code change. Matching is case-insensitive per RFC 9309.

page_selection._note: max_pages is a budget-derived MAXIMUM, not a guarantee. Pages skipped for budget yield `unknown` checks (excluded from the denominator), so a short scan lowers confidence rather than the score.
page_selection._language_neutrality: Selection is STRUCTURAL, never lexical: we do NOT match /about, /faq etc. — that is English-only and silently degrades to homepage-only on any non-English site. Pages are ranked by nav membership and URL depth, which behave identically in every language.

language._note: Checks with requires_language=true resolve to `unknown` (never `fail`) when detection is absent or the language is unsupported. Without this gate, every non-English site would produce a wall of false positives.

render._note: Tier A = real Chromium render. Tier B = browserless SPA heuristic when no browser is available. Disclosed via diagnostics.render_mode. Chromium is provisioned as a SETUP step, never inside the timed run.
render._viewport_note: Desktop 1280x800. Height matches first_viewport_px in checks.json — these two MUST stay in sync or the above-the-fold engagement checks measure a different box than they render.
render._wait_until_note: MUST NOT be networkidle. That state needs 500ms with <=2 connections in flight, which analytics beacons, chat widgets and long-polling never allow, so it does not fire and the whole render budget is spent waiting. Measured on python.org: load 1.2s, domcontentloaded 3.9s, networkidle 20.0s then timeout. Network quiescence is pursued separately, bounded by network_quiet_ms, and its expiry is recorded, never raised.
render._budget_note: nav_timeout_ms + network_quiet_ms + settle_ms are all clamped inside max_render_ms, which is itself clamped by the global deadline. A navigation timeout SALVAGES the DOM rather than discarding it: the milestone failing to fire does not mean the page is absent.
render._tier_b_note: Tier-B signals used when no browser is available. These are POSITIVE EVIDENCE of client-side rendering, never a requirement: a site that matches none of them is not penalised, it simply yields a lower-confidence result. Markers are in config so new frameworks need no code change.
